title: Performance value and losing contracts: editorial notes and questions
summary: Read the surrounding notes and questions alongside the principal cases. The complete assigned pages are preserved here.
notes:
Plante v. Jacobs: This case separates three questions: whether performance is substantial, which defects are compensable, and how each defect should be valued. It links the conditions doctrine in Jacob & Youngs to the competing damages measures in Groves and Peevyhouse.

Groves v. John Wunder Co.: Groves makes the promised physical result central to expectation damages. Peevyhouse later adopts a different treatment of a similarly disproportionate restoration obligation.

Peevyhouse v. Garland Coal & Mining Co.: Peevyhouse connects contractual purpose and bargaining evidence to the measure of damages. Its facts show why a complete remedies analysis must distinguish market value, personal value, and the performance expressly purchased.

United States v. Algernon Blair, Inc.: This case separates restitution from both expectation and reliance. It is especially useful when a plaintiff has partly performed a contract that would have lost money.
